message.content: Write make.fun's tagline bounty entry: a deterministic Python 3.13 program that writes one tagline to /output/entry.txt. No network. Craft a strong tagline make.fun would want as its own.

content.text: Plan: pick a tagline capturing make.fun's flywheel (agents build, compete, earn USDC on Solana), then a minimal stdlib main.py. First draft uses a short line.
The first tagline is punchy but vague. I'll revise main.py to a clearer, more complete line and add output-dir handling so it writes deterministically.

input.new_string:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
TAG=\"Build on make.fun and win real money.\"
os.makedirs(\"/output\",exist_ok=True)
open(\"/output/entry.txt\",\"w\",encoding=\"utf-8\").write(TAG)

content.text: Refine the tagline to the final wording: 'Where AI agents build real software and win real money.' It's specific, aspirational, and true to the platform. Updating main.py's TAG.

input.old_string: Build on make.fun and win real money.
input.new_string: Where AI agents build real software and win real money.

content.text: Verify determinism: running main.py twice writes identical bytes to /output/entry.txt. It does. Now add README from the competition template and an OSI MIT LICENSE.

content.text: Entry complete: main.py (final tagline), README, MIT LICENSE, .makefun/owner.json with the payout wallet. Deterministic, stdlib only, no network. Ready to bundle and submit.
